subChunks.title: Lists, Feeds, and List Items
subChunks.hookHtml: Lists appear in nearly every UI — navigation menus, activity feeds, search results, notification panels, and settings pages. The challenge is making each item scannable: clear information hierarchy, proper image/text alignment, interaction states, and consistent spacing across variable-length content.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
List container patterns

/* Divided list */
<ul class="divide-y divide-gray-100 bg-white rounded-xl">

/* Card list (each item is its own card) */
<ul class="space-y-3">

/* Compact list (tight spacing) */
<ul class="space-y-1">

Standard list item anatomy

<li class="flex items-start gap-4 px-4 py-3 hover:bg-gray-50 transition-colors cursor-pointer">
  <!-- Avatar -->
  <img class="w-10 h-10 rounded-full flex-none mt-0.5" src="..." alt="" />

  <!-- Content -->
  <div class="flex-1 min-w-0">  <!-- min-w-0 enables truncation inside flex -->
    <div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
      <span class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 truncate">Aria Sunforge</span>
      <time class="text-xs text-gray-400 flex-none">2h ago</time>
    </div>
    <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-0.5 line-clamp-2">Completed the Dragon Quest...</p>
  </div>
</li>

The min-w-0 rule for flex children

By default, flex items won't shrink below their minimum content size. This prevents truncate from working on text inside a flex item. Adding min-w-0 to the flex item allows it to shrink, enabling truncation.

/* Without min-w-0: truncate doesn't work, text overflows */
<div class="flex-1">
  <p class="truncate">Very long text that won't truncate...</p>
</div>

/* With min-w-0: truncate works correctly */
<div class="flex-1 min-w-0">
  <p class="truncate">Very long text that will truncate</p>
</div>

Activity feed item

<li class="flex gap-3 py-4">
  <!-- Timeline dot -->
  <div class="relative flex-none mt-1">
    <div class="w-2 h-2 rounded-full bg-blue-500"></div>
    <!-- Vertical line connecting items -->
    <div class="absolute top-2 bottom-0 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 w-px bg-gray-200"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="flex-1 min-w-0 pb-4">
    <p class="text-sm text-gray-900">Aria completed <strong>Dragon Quest</strong></p>
    <time class="text-xs text-gray-400 mt-0.5 block">2 hours ago</time>
  </div>
</li>

Empty list state

<div class="py-12 text-center">
  <div class="text-4xl mb-3">🗺️</div>
  <p class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900">No quests yet</p>
  <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-1">Start a quest to see it here.</p>
  <button class="mt-4 px-4 py-2 bg-blue-600 text-white text-sm font-medium rounded-md">
    Browse Quests
  </button>
</div>

Lyra: "min-w-0 on flex children is one of the most commonly forgotten utilities in Tailwind. The moment you put truncate on text inside a flex item and it doesn't work — add min-w-0 to the parent. Flex items default to min-width: auto, which prevents them from shrinking below their content. min-w-0 overrides this."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: A list item must be scannable in under a second. Avatar or icon on the left. Primary text in bold. Secondary text smaller and muted. Timestamp right-aligned. Action on hover. This is not opinion — it is the pattern every human being has learned from years of email clients and social feeds.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a notification feed with proper list item anatomy:

  • .feed: divide-y, divide-gray-100, bg-white, rounded-xl, border, border-gray-100
  • .feed-item: flex, items-start, gap-4, px-4, py-3, hover:bg-gray-50, transition-colors, cursor-pointer
  • .feed-avatar: w-10, h-10, rounded-full, flex-none
  • .feed-content: flex-1, min-w-0
  • .feed-name: text-sm, font-medium, text-gray-900, truncate
  • .feed-time: text-xs, text-gray-400, flex-none
  • .feed-text: text-sm, text-gray-500, mt-0.5, line-clamp-2

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a search results list from scratch: each item shows a thumbnail image, a title (truncated to one line), a URL (truncated, muted colour), and a description (clamped to two lines). Add a hover state, an empty state message when there are no results, and a 'Load more' button at the bottom. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the min-w-0 rule — why does truncate fail inside a flex item without it, and what does min-w-0 actually set in CSS? Walk through the flex items-start gap-4 pattern for list items — why items-start rather than items-center, and why gap-4 rather than margin?

questions.prompt: A list item has flex layout and a text span with truncate, but the text never truncates — it overflows the container. Which class on the text's parent div fixes this?
options: min-w-0 — overrides the default min-width: auto on flex items, allowing them to shrink and enabling truncation
flex-shrink — allows the element to shrink
questions.answer: min-w-0 — overrides the default min-width: auto on flex items, allowing them to shrink and enabling truncation
questions.explanation: Flex items have min-width: auto by default, which means they won't shrink below their content's natural width. This prevents truncate from working because the element never becomes narrower than the text. min-w-0 sets min-width: 0, allowing the flex item to shrink to zero, which then allows overflow: hidden (from truncate) to actually clip the text.

questions.prompt: A divided list uses divide-y divide-gray-100 on the ul. But the last list item also has a bottom border from the divide-y. Which Tailwind variant removes the bottom border from the last item?
options: divide-y doesn't add a border to the last item — only between items
questions.answer: divide-y doesn't add a border to the last item — only between items
questions.explanation: divide-y adds a border-top to every child element except the first one (using the :not(:first-child) selector). This creates dividers between items but not after the last one. There's no trailing border to remove — divide-y already handles this correctly by design.

questions.prompt: A list item uses items-center to vertically align an avatar with multi-line text. The avatar appears centred against the text block. Which alignment variant would produce more natural reading alignment for multi-line text?
options: items-start — aligns the avatar with the top of the text block, which looks more natural for multi-line content
items-baseline — aligns avatar bottom with text baseline
items-stretch — stretches the avatar to match text height
items-center is always correct for list items
questions.answer: items-start — aligns the avatar with the top of the text block, which looks more natural for multi-line content
questions.explanation: items-center vertically centres the avatar against the full height of the text block. For a two-line text block, this positions the avatar in the middle of both lines. items-start aligns the avatar with the top line, which is more natural — the eye connects the avatar with the first line (the name), not the centre of the content block. For single-line content, items-center is fine.
